contract_clause: SymbolicCode::from_static() validates against CODE_REGISTRY
domain_claim: SymbolicCode constructed from a registered string returns Some; all unregistered strings return None
notes: Critical invariant: the SymbolicCode type must never contain an unregistered string. Kani proof: for all strings, from_static(s).is_some() iff s is in CODE_REGISTRY. Proptest: generate valid/invalid strings, assert correspondence.

contract_clause: CODE_REGISTRY has no duplicate symbolic names and no duplicate numeric codes
domain_claim: The code registry is a bijection: each symbolic name maps to a unique numeric code, and each numeric code maps to a unique symbolic name
notes: Const assertion at compile time covers this. Runtime test as defense-in-depth. Kani can verify at const-eval time.

contract_clause: SymbolicCode↔DiagnosticCode round-trip is bijective
domain_claim: For every code in the registry, SymbolicCode→numeric and numeric→SymbolicCode is an identity round-trip
notes: Round-trip property: from_static(s).unwrap().numeric_code() == registry[s] AND DiagnosticCode(registry[s]).symbolic_code() == Some(s).

contract_clause: ValidationError::code() uses exhaustive match without wildcard
domain_claim: Every ValidationError variant (58 total) maps to exactly one SymbolicCode and the match is exhaustive
notes: Exhaustive match is enforced by Rust compiler. Kani proof: for each variant, code() returns a SymbolicCode that is in the registry and produces a non-zero numeric code.

contract_clause: Every ValidationError variant produces a unique SymbolicCode
domain_claim: No two ValidationError variants share the same symbolic diagnostic code
notes: 58 variants → 58 unique codes. Proptest: enumerate all variants, collect codes, assert set size == 58. Existing test all_variants_have_unique_diagnostic_codes does this for numeric; needs to be extended for symbolic.

contract_clause: is_supported_code() accepts E05xx, E06xx, and codes above 0x401B
domain_claim: All numeric code constants defined in vb_validate, vb_storage, and vb_runtime are accepted by is_supported_code()
notes: Kani: for each code constant in the workspace, assert is_supported_code(CONST). Proptest: parse E0501, E0601, E401C and assert success.

contract_clause: Diagnostic.numeric_code.symbolic_code() == Some(Diagnostic.code)
domain_claim: Every Diagnostic record has consistent symbolic and numeric codes — the numeric is derived from and consistent with the symbolic
notes: Constructor-only invariant: Diagnostic::new() derives numeric_code from code. Kani proof: for any valid SymbolicCode, constructing a Diagnostic yields self-consistent fields.

contract_clause: YamlError::code() returns a valid SymbolicCode for all 20 variants
domain_claim: Every YamlError variant maps to a SymbolicCode in the registry
notes: New feature: YamlError currently has no code() method. Kani proof: for each variant, code().is_some() and the code is in the registry.

contract_clause: All CompileError symbolic codes are registered in CODE_REGISTRY
domain_claim: The 30+ symbolic strings emitted by CompileError::code() (including compilation-specific codes like INVALID_EXPRESSION) are all in the registry
notes: CompileError currently emits some codes not in Section 16 (e.g., UNKNOWN_INPUT_SCHEMA_FIELD). These must be added to the registry. Proptest: enumerate all CompileError variants, assert code() is in registry.

contract_clause: SymbolicCode and DiagnosticCode construction and operations are zero-allocation
domain_claim: No heap allocation occurs during SymbolicCode construction, copy, display, or numeric code resolution
notes: SymbolicCode is Copy (repr(transparent) over &str). DiagnosticCode is Copy (repr(transparent) over u16). Kani stubs for alloc can verify no allocation path is reached.

contract_clause: Backward compatibility: DiagnosticCode::from_str("E0101") still works
domain_claim: Existing numeric code parsing is preserved; all previously supported codes still parse; E0501/E0601/E401C now also parse
notes: Breaking change risk. Kani proof: for all previously supported codes (E0101-E040C, E1001-E401B), assert from_str succeeds. For all newly added codes (E0501-E0603, E401C+), assert from_str succeeds.

contract_clause: SymbolicCode serialization/deserialization round-trips and rejects unknown codes
domain_claim: Serialize produces the symbolic string; Deserialize validates against registry and rejects unknown strings
notes: Dual risk: valid codes must round-trip; unknown codes must be rejected. Fuzz target: arbitrary JSON with 'code' field, assert deserialization either succeeds with valid SymbolicCode or fails with error.

contract_clause: All registered numeric codes are non-zero
domain_claim: No diagnostic code in the registry has numeric value 0x0000
notes: Zero code is reserved as 'no error' sentinel. Const assertion at compile time.

contract_clause: Each registry entry's category matches its numeric high byte
domain_claim: For each CodeEntry, (numeric >> 8) & 0xFF matches the expected high-byte range for its CodeCategory
notes: E.g., all Schema codes have high byte 0x01. Gate codes have 0x05. This enables category-based filtering. Const assertion at compile time.

contract_clause: DiagnosticCode::symbolic_code() reverse-lookup is correct
domain_claim: For any DiagnosticCode with a numeric value in the registry, symbolic_code() returns the matching SymbolicCode. For values outside the registry, returns None.
notes: Reverse-lookup. Kani: for each code in registry, DiagnosticCode(code).symbolic_code() == Some(expected). For a value outside registry, returns None.

contract_clause: All 36 Section 16 symbolic codes match master contract exactly
domain_claim: The 36 codes from Section 16 (DUPLICATE_KEY through HTTP_TRIGGER_OUT_OF_CORE) are present in the registry and map to their correct numeric encodings
notes: Contract parity. Proptest: define expected mapping from master doc, assert registry contains exact matches. Test must fail if master doc is updated but registry is not.

contract_clause: HasSymbolicCode::symbolic_code() implementations are pure, total, deterministic
domain_claim: For any error value, calling symbolic_code() twice returns the same SymbolicCode; never panics; no I/O
notes: Determinism is critical: error codes must be stable across calls. Kani: for arbitrary error value, assert symbolic_code() returns the same result on repeated calls.

contract_clause: Diagnostic record invariant: no mismatched symbolic/numeric codes
domain_claim: It is impossible to construct a Diagnostic record where numeric_code.symbolic_code() != Some(code)
notes: Make illegal state unrepresentable. Only constructor can create Diagnostic; it derives numeric_code deterministically. Kani proof on constructor.

contract_clause: CoreError, RuntimeError, JournalError all have symbolic_code() returning valid SymbolicCode
domain_claim: Every variant of CoreError (46), RuntimeError (25+), and JournalError (28) maps to a registered SymbolicCode
notes: Existing diagnostic_code() returns numeric; new symbolic_code() must be added. Proptest: enumerate all variants in each error type, assert symbolic_code() is in registry.

contract_clause: diag_codes.rs constants promoted from #[cfg(test)] to public and synchronized with registry
domain_claim: The 58 numeric code constants in vb_validate/src/diag_codes.rs are public, non-test-only, and match the registry
notes: Currently test-only. Must be promoted. Proptest: for each constant, assert it exists in registry with correct symbolic name. Ensures no drift between constants file and registry.
